stimulus.description: An inch ruler and a centimeter ruler drawn at true scale, with an object laid next to both. The tutor can set the object length.
must_show_exactly: Inch ruler with equal inch marks
Centimeter ruler with equal centimeter marks, true to inch scale
One inch is longer than one centimeter, about 2.5 times
Object ends line up with the right marks: pencil about 7 inches and about 18 centimeters
stimulus.alt_text: An inch ruler and a centimeter ruler next to a pencil.

questions.prompt: One bookmark measures about 3 inches and about 8 centimeters. A centimeter is smaller than an inch. Think about how many smaller units cover the same bookmark. Which measurement uses more units? Say 1 for inches or 2 for centimeters.
The same toy is about 4 inches long and about 10 centimeters long. Its length stays the same. An inch is bigger than a centimeter. Use this key: 1 means inches and 2 means centimeters.

parts.prompt: Choose the larger unit from the key. What number names that unit?
Use your choice of larger unit. Smaller units need more repeats to cover the toy. What number names the unit with more repeats?
Check using the measured counts instead of unit size. Compare the 4 units with the 10 units. What number from the key names the measurement with more units?

hints.text: Compare unit sizes for the same object.

Smaller pieces take more repeats to cover the same length. Give both the size reason and the count effect.
The bookmark stays the same length when units change.
Smaller centimeters need more repeats than bigger inches.
Compare the count of eight with three and use the named unit key.
Choose by unit size, predict the unit count, then check using the measured counts.

For part 3, compare the four inch units and ten centimeter units without converting either measurement.

input_contract.authoritative_rules: Use v0.2 route definitions and per-question guidance. Resolve concept_card references against the linked concept; do not invent missing questions, assets, answers, or hints.

attempt_policy.repeated_unclear: Count one incorrect attempt and take that question's incorrect route.
attempt_policy.at_parent_limit: If correct, advance. Otherwise reveal all required answers with worked steps and advance; do not launch another follow-up or retry.
attempt_policy.at_followup_limit: If incorrect or repeatedly unclear, reveal the follow-up answer; then return to the parent if it has an attempt left, otherwise reveal the parent and advance.

outcome_classification.single_answer: Compare with the linked rubric. Use partial only when that rubric explicitly permits it. If no answer can be understood, use unclear.

multi_part_rules.unclear: No part can be understood, or a supplied part remains ambiguous. Reprompt only the ambiguous part when another part is understood.
multi_part_rules.incomplete: At least one part is understood, no supplied part is ambiguous, and one or more required parts are missing.
multi_part_rules.correct: All required parts are present and match their answer keys.
multi_part_rules.partial: All required parts are understood and present, and some but not all match. Keep correct parts and retry only incorrect parts.
multi_part_rules.incorrect: All required parts are understood and present, and none match.

outcome_classification.open_response: Accept equivalent wording that meets the linked rubric's correct description. Use its partial description only when explicitly present; do not require an exact wording for an open answer.
outcome_classification.normalization: Trim surrounding whitespace and punctuation and ignore letter case. Use the declared rubric accept variants. A clear unambiguous number with the question's unit can be compared as a number; ambiguous or conflicting numbers require a reprompt.

hint_policy.sequence_source: Use each question's hint_sequence in order; source_hint_refs are provenance, not an additional delivery sequence.
hint_policy.delivery: Give one hint at a time. Never reveal a later hint automatically.
hint_policy.on_help: Give the next unused hint without consuming an attempt, then repeat the pending question or retry parts.
hint_policy.after_last_hint: Repeat the last hint and reprompt the pending question without consuming an attempt for help. Reveal only after the attempt limit or an explicit request for the answer.
hint_policy.on_answer_requested: Reveal worked steps, then advance for a main question or return to its parent for a follow-up.
hint_policy.partial_or_incomplete: Keep correct parts. Read only unresolved part prompts; do not ask the learner to redo correct parts.

silence_policy.after_reprompt: A second silence counts as an incorrect attempt. Follow the question's incorrect route.

route_definitions.advance_to_next_question_or_close: Advance through delivery_order; close after the final main question.
route_definitions.retry_eligible_parts_with_hint_until_max: Give next hint and retry only unresolved parts if attempts remain; otherwise reveal and advance.
route_definitions.hint_then_retry_until_max_attempts: Give next hint and retry if attempts remain; otherwise reveal and advance.
route_definitions.reprompt_once_then_treat_as_incorrect: One clarification without an attempt; repeated unclear counts as incorrect and follows the current question's incorrect route.
route_definitions.followup_once_then_retry_parent_if_attem: Give next parent hint, ask its follow_up_ref once, then retry parent if attempts remain; otherwise reveal parent and advance. If already used, hint and retry without another follow-up.
route_definitions.followup_once_then_retry_missing_parts_i: Give next parent hint, ask its follow_up_ref once, then retry only missing or incorrect parts if attempts remain; otherwise reveal and advance. If already used, retry missing or incorrect parts without another follow-up.
route_definitions.return_to_parent_if_attempt_remains_else: Return to triggered_by.question_id while preserving attempts and correct parts. Retry unresolved parts if an attempt remains; otherwise reveal parent and advance.
route_definitions.reveal_followup_then_return_to_parent_if: Reveal the follow-up with worked steps, then return to triggered_by.question_id if attempts remain; otherwise reveal parent and advance.
